result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the schema uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]` inside z.object. In JS, `z.string().toString()` evaluates at object-literal construction to the string '[object Object]', so z.object gets literal keys '[object Object]' (a required number) — not wildcard keys. Every real token response lacks these fields, so safeParse fails and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' for all sync-endpoint responses. The mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to express “any string key with a number value” via computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`. In JS this becomes a single literal property name (whatever `toString()` returns for the Zod object, commonly "[object Object]"), not a wildcard. As a result, the schema will require that one specific (nonsensical) key to be present as a number, causing `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` to reject normal token responses when sync is enabled. Zod wildcard behavior would need `.catchall(...)`, `.passthrough()`, or a `z.record(...)` approach instead.
